Sentence (English): #SamsungElectronicsEventParticipation.
Comments (English): #SamsungElectronicsEventParticipation. During the purchase process, there was absolutely no information provided regarding the fact that switching the dishwasher panel to glass makes the door heavier and causes it to open wide during automatic operation. The only explanation given was that glass is scratch-resistant. From a user's perspective, while aesthetics are important, it would be nice to be informed about these small details as well. Since all my kitchen appliances are high-gloss glass products, I bought this one to match. Your supporting documentation was not provided or the documentation you provided does not meet the requirements. Please review the claim documentation requirements, log into your claim, and attach a new document to your existing claim." My first guess as to what information wasn't available was the fact I used the allowed FD numbers instead of the serial number. I included those as best I could; good luck with that on the microhoods since they don't have a serial number. Had I known the rebate was a bait and switch, I would have purchased these appliances elsewhere.

Most importantly though, it actually does an outstanding job cleaning. Plates, glasses, silverware & pans have all come out spotless, even when we have loaded it up with dried-on food. The PrecisionWash system does a great job, and the PowerControl feature is useful when one section of the load needs some extra cleaning power. The CrystalDry feature has also impressed me because even our plastic containers come out noticeably drier instead of being covered in water like they often were with the LG. The rack system is another major improvement--the racks feel solid, glide smoothly & offer plenty of adjustment for larger dishes, pots and awkward items. The third rack gives us a lot more usable space for silverware, spatulas, lids & smaller items that used to take up room elsewhere. I also appreciate the stainless-steel interior, fingerprint-resistant exterior and AquaStop leak protection. Overall, this Bosch feels much better engineered than our old LG. It is quieter, cleans better, dries better, holds more & simply feels like a higher-quality appliance. Sentence (English): Super Quiet.
Comments (English): [ Bosch delivers a quality product here. ] || ---------------- || Super Quiet. Cleaning appears to be better than the LG we had and I loved how it cleaned. Sure, plastic might be damp when cycle is finished, but everything else is dry and I don't have to worry about warped plastic as much. WiFi connection fought me for a while, then suddenly was fine. The app and instructions via the app are super helpful. We got used to the controls on the front so we could see what the old dishwasher was doing, but we are adjusting to the cleaner look and the lack of random turning the unit on because we were leaning for a something above it. I would have given this a 5, but the door feels flimsy, and the front of the silverware tray pops off often when trying to move that rack in or out (it's the center part of the rack and even looks like it was designed to be a pull). I think we can get more dishes in this than before (great capacity), but we had to learn how to place the dishes to get the maximum fit. Overall, we don't even know it's running it's so quiet, and the dishes are shinier than before, (there are no spots and we don't even use a rinse agent, just pods) and although it was pricier than we would like we are anticipating a long life out of this since the mother in laws Bosch has been around for a long time.

Comments (English): [ A dishwasher becomes more necessary as you get older ] || ---------------- || Twenty years ago, I tried a Miele dishwasher and was so disappointed that I thought, "Wow, I'll never buy a dishwasher in my life!" But after much hesitation while moving this time, I finally decided to buy one. I'm fast at washing dishes, so I wondered if I was making a mistake I would regret. It doesn't drastically change my life. However, on days when I don't feel like doing anything, I can just toss the dishes into the dishwasher and say goodbye to the chores that weigh me down like homework. Even if it only reduces my kitchen work by 10%, I think it's a worthwhile choice. I'm still not very good at Tetris, so I'm working on it, but once I get used to it, I might become a huge fan of dishwashers.

Comments (English): [ I received a different model. It is not the model I ordered. ] || ---------------- || I purchased the DW99F79E1 model and completed the payment on May 24th. I specifically selected and purchased the model, expecting to receive it immediately. I waited a total of 47 days for delivery. In particular, over the course of about two weeks from the scheduled delivery date, the delivery date was set, canceled, or changed a total of six times. Each time, my son or I waited for the delivery on the promised date, but the delivery continued to be postponed. As a result, there were times when I was unable to work on scheduled dates, leading to financial loss. When I finally received the product, it was shipped without packaging. Furthermore, no one informed me that the model had been changed. Therefore, I could not have known that a different model had been delivered immediately after shipment. In addition, I was not provided with any dishwasher user manual or related documents. I can only interpret this as an attempt to hide the product's model information to prevent me from immediately verifying it or returning it right away. Even after installation was completed, I did not receive any instructions on how to connect the product to the smartphone application. To be clear, no one informed me of the model change at the time of installation, and as a result, I came to believe incorrect information. It was only after my son personally connected the dishwasher to a mobile application that I realized the installed product was not the one I ordered. I had ordered the DW99F79E1 model, but the product actually delivered and installed was the DW90F79F1 model. Although I am not a tech expert, I can clearly tell that the two models are different. I cannot understand why no one informed me of the model change in advance, especially since I paid for and purchased the exact model I wanted. Furthermore, I actually used the dishwasher before realizing that the delivered product was not what I ordered, but I was not satisfied with the cleaning performance. Dirt remained on the cups even after washing, and the drying performance was also very poor. For these reasons, I believe they did not show me the product packaging, did not provide the user manual, and did not inform me that the model had been changed. I am currently demanding the return of this delivered dishwasher and a full refund of the purchase price. I am not satisfied with this replacement model.

Sentence (English): I reviewed this dishwasher earlier and received a generic customer service response.
Comments (English): [ Generic Samsung Response - Customer Service Complaint ] || ---------------- || I reviewed this dishwasher earlier and received a generic customer service response. They want me to reach out but all the links are generic. We've finally submitted a complaint to the Illinois Attorney General about our experiences. If Samsung wants to know (which they don't) here's the complaint: . The dishwasher was diagnosed by an authorized technician as having a failed drain pump. The repair provider said they had obtained the part and was ready to repair it. Samsung canceled the repair and directed us into a replacement process. We were not given a choice. No option to use a local retailer, and required use of Samsung's e-coupon system and its own network of fulfillment, delivery, installation, and haul-away contractors. Pricing discrepancies: e-coupon did not cover replacement cost. The original shopping cart totaled $1,333.14 (unit $999, discounted from $1,299, plus delivery/installation $187.97, plus tax $94.17). After applying the required e-coupon ($1,260), the balance should have been $73.14. Instead it became $258.21, then $321.65 on the final receipt — more than four times the correct amount, with no explanation. We were required to pay this in full to proceed, and Samsung opened a separate reimbursement claim that remains outstanding. Resolving this required a single call of approximately three hours, plus numerous other calls and transfers. Delivery failures: The replacement was ordered with installation and haul-away included. The original June 4 delivery date was delayed to June 11 due to Samsung's once-weekly delivery schedule (shipped only from Chicago 275 miles from our home). On June 11, the delivery crew was not qualified to perform the installation or haul-away, despite both being clearly marked on the order. The supervisor only offered a reschedule to June 17, with no assurance a qualified crew would be sent. Because the old unit could not be removed and the new one could not be installed, we declined delivery. Failed escalation to executive customer service: After the initial failures described above, we escalated to Samsung's CEO via email. A Case Manager was assigned from Samsung's Extra Care team, and we provided all requested information and documentation. Despite this, the pricing discrepancy and delivery/installation failures remained unresolved. The June 11 delivery failure occurred after this escalation had already begun. More than 35 days (new dishwasher installed 42 days) after opening the claim, despite executive escalation, Samsung has still not provided a functioning dishwasher. Samsung directed us away from repair, into its own replacement process, charged us over four times the correct amount with no explanation, and twice delayed delivery. Once for its own scheduling reasons, and again by sending an unqualified crew. For comparison, a Frigidaire warranty replacement last year, handled through a local retailer credit system, was completed within days of authorization. Samsung's process has now taken over a month with no resolution.

Comments (English): [ Stay away from Lowe's dishwashers ] || ---------------- || Do not buy a dishwasher from Lowe's. Save yourself the hassle. We purchased this dishwasher on 6/4/26. We called Lowe's for resolution and they referred us to a third party company called Appliance Repair Done Better to look at our dishwasher. Mind you, I still haven't to make payments in a dishwasher that is completely broken. I am absolutely furious!

Sentence (English): Owned a KitchenAid dishwasher for 6 years that began having issues draining.
Comments (English): [ Great replacement for "luxury" dishwasher ] || ---------------- || Owned a KitchenAid dishwasher for 6 years that began having issues draining. I picked this dishwasher after reading reviews and consulting consumer reports. Overall, I am very happy with this dishwasher. We have had it for a week and find that it cleans dishes well. About 30 minutes prior to the cycle being complete, the door will openly slightly to facilitate better drying. Some do have a little water but nothing more than what would be reasonable expected. The walls and floor of the dishwasher are always dry which is great to prevent any water from sitting between cycles. The dishwasher is fairly loud in the beginning of the cycle. However, the majority of the washing cycle noise level is reasonable. I like the filter on this model. The KitchenAid had a plastic basket filter with large grooves which allowed smaller food particles to pash through and get into the pumps of the dishwasher. This machine has a fine metal mesh filter which is easy to remove and clean under the sink faucet. Even after one cycle I could the see residue of what it had filtered from the pumps of the dishwasher. This dishwasher was easy to install. There are channels underneath the dishwasher which makes pulling the electrical line much easier than my previous model. The rear leveling leg is a great addition as it makes leveling the dishwasher straightforward. Even though this dishwasher is louder than my previous model, I like this model as it was a fair price, does a great job cleaning the dishes, and leaves them dry.

Sentence (English): I'll start with the bad- and that mainly involves the installation.
Comments (English): [ Frustrating installation, but happy it's here! ] || ---------------- || I'll start with the bad- and that mainly involves the installation. As I waited for my purchase to arrive, I read through the preparation documents and felt sufficiently prepared to install this dishwasher. However, as I started the installation I ran into lots of issues. They don't disclose very clearly what parts you'll need ahead of time unless you've read through the instruction manual. So I was missing essential parts necessary to complete the install. It felt misleading if them to not clearly explain that you'll need to buy a packet of equipment from them to make it work. Seems like something that should absolutely be included with the dishwasher. After completing the first few installation steps, I found the instructions confusing and a bit unclear. Ultimately, I had to call a professional with over 50 years of experience to help complete the installation. I should have paid for LG to install it upon delivery because it isn't easy without a professional. When I tried to call and see if I could pay to have one of their people come out, they said they don't offer that service after delivery and I had to find a handyman on my own. So the entire installation experience was difficult, and very frustrating. Now that the dishwasher is actually installed, it is excellent! The one hour wash is so helpful, because I have two kids and a steam of constant dishes to wash. You can download an app to change sound settings, and create custom wash cycles. I really like the adjustable middle rack, as sometimes I need it longer for baby bottles. It is SO quiet. Which is wonderful because my house is already so noisy, and previously I had a very loud dishwasher I couldn't have a conversation around. The steam feature that opens is nice in a way, but the amount of steam that comes out concerns me because I am worried it will damage the surrounding wood, despite the protective tape they included, so I may turn that feature off in the future.All in all, a Hi-Tech dishwasher that works quickly, quietly, and efficiently. The install process was extremely frustrating (hence the missing star), but the dishwasher itself is a great appliance.

Sentence (English): When moving, the kitchen appliance I agonized over the most was the dishwasher.
Comments (English): When moving, the kitchen appliance I agonized over the most was the dishwasher. Built-in models required custom-built base cabinets, which was a hassle and took up awkward space. However, I heard there were countertop models that sit right on the counter, so after a frantic search, I decided on the Bespoke. To start with the conclusion, I am so satisfied that I wonder why I didn't buy it sooner! 1. Design and Space Utilization (White is the way to go!) As expected from Bespoke, the design is incredibly clean and pretty. It doesn't detract from the kitchen interior; instead, it brightens up the space. I was worried that the 6-place setting might be too big, but placing it on one side of the sink makes it fit perfectly, like custom-made furniture. The white color makes the kitchen look spacious and is the epitome of cleanliness. 2. Capacity and Storage (Sufficient for a family of four!) If you think of it as only suitable for a single person living alone just because it's a 6-place setting, you're mistaken. The interior space is deeper and more efficiently organized than expected. If you arrange rice bowls, soup bowls, pots, and pans in the bottom section, quite a lot fits inside. The top section has a separate space to spread out cutlery and cooking utensils, ensuring they don't get tangled and are cleaned thoroughly. It fits all the dishes left after a family meal in one go. 3. Washing and Drying Performance. The most important factor is washing power, and it cleans much more thoroughly and leaves a squeaky clean finish than hand washing. Even greasy grilled meat dishes or pots with burnt-on sauce disappear without a trace if you put them in after just a light pre-wash. Since it uses high-temperature washing, it feels like it is sterilizing, so I feel much more at ease regarding hygiene. If you leave the door open after it is finished, it dries completely and is spotless. 4. Satisfaction with Rocket Installation Service. I ordered via Coupang Rocket Installation, but it was delayed by about two days, which was a bit disappointing. Overall Review and Recommendation. However, I heard there were countertop models that sit right on the counter, so after a frantic search, I decided on the Bespoke. To start with the conclusion, I am so satisfied that I wonder why I didn't buy it sooner! 1. Design and Space Utilization (White is the way to go!) As expected from Bespoke, the design is incredibly clean and pretty. It doesn't detract from the kitchen interior; instead, it brightens up the space. I was worried that the 6-place setting might be too big, but placing it on one side of the sink makes it fit perfectly, like custom-made furniture. The white color makes the kitchen look spacious and is the epitome of cleanliness. 2. Capacity and Storage (Sufficient for a family of four!) If you think of it as only suitable for a single person living alone just because it's a 6-place setting, you're mistaken. The interior space is deeper and more efficiently organized than expected. If you arrange rice bowls, soup bowls, pots, and pans in the bottom section, quite a lot fits inside. The top section has a separate space to spread out cutlery and cooking utensils, ensuring they don't get tangled and are cleaned thoroughly. It fits all the dishes left after a family meal in one go. 3. Washing and Drying Performance. The most important factor is washing power, and it cleans much more thoroughly and leaves a squeaky clean finish than hand washing. Even greasy grilled meat dishes or pots with burnt-on sauce disappear without a trace if you put them in after just a light pre-wash. Since it uses high-temperature washing, it feels like it is sterilizing, so I feel much more at ease regarding hygiene. If you leave the door open after it is finished, it dries completely and is spotless. 4. Satisfaction with Rocket Installation Service. I ordered via Coupang Rocket Installation, but it was delayed by about two days, which was a bit disappointing. Overall Review and Recommendation. Since dishwashing time has decreased, I have more personal time after meals, and my quality of life as a housewife has skyrocketed. I recommend this to those who find built-in installation burdensome, those who want to keep their kitchen interior bright and cheerful, and those who want to escape the hell of dishwashing!
Comments (Original): 이사하면서 주방 가전 중 가장 고민했던 게 식기세척기였어요. 빌트인은 싱크대 하부장을 짜야 해서 번거롭고 공간도 애매했는데, 싱크대 위에 올려두고 쓰는 카운터탑 모델이 있다고 해서 폭풍 검색 끝에 비스포크로 결정했습니다. 결론부터 말씀드리면 '왜 이제 샀나' 싶을 정도로 대만족입니다!​1. 디자인 및 공간 활용 (화이트는 진리!)​역시 비스포크답게 디자인이 정말 깔끔하고 예쁩니다. 주방 인테리어를 해치지 않고 오히려 화사해진 느낌이에요. 6인용이라 너무 크지 않을까 걱정했는데, 싱크대 한쪽에 올리니 맞춤 가구처럼 딱 들어맞네요. 화이트 컬러라 주방이 넓어 보이고 깔끔함 그 자체입니다.​2. 용량 및 수납력 (4인 가족도 충분!)​6인용이라고 해서 자취생용 정도로 생각하시면 오산이에요. 생각보다 내부 공간이 깊고 알차게 구성되어 있습니다.​아래쪽엔 밥공기, 국그릇, 냄비나 프라이팬까지 요리조리 배치하면 꽤 많이 들어가요.​상단에는 수저나 조리도구를 펼쳐놓을 수 있는 공간이 따로 있어서 엉키지 않고 깨끗하게 세척됩니다.가족들이 한 끼 먹고 난 후의 설거지거리는 한 번에 다 들어가는 수준이에요.​3. 세척력 및 건조 성능​제일 중요한 건 세척력인데, 손설거지보다 훨씬 깨끗하고 뽀득뽀득하게 닦입니다. 기름기 많은 고기 구워 먹은 접시나 양념이 눌어붙은 냄비도 애벌설거지 살짝만 해서 넣으면 흔적도 없이 번쩍번쩍해져요. 고온 세척이라 살균되는 기분이라 위생적으로도 훨씬 안심이 됩니다. 완료된 후에 문을 열어두면 물기 없이 뽀송하게 말라 있어요.​4. 로켓설치 서비스 만족도​쿠팡 로켓설치로 주문했지만 이틀정도 지연되어 조금 아쉬웠어요.​ 총평 및 추천설거지 시간이 줄어드니까 식사 후에 개인 시간도 늘어나고 주부 삶의 질이 수직 상승했습니다.​빌트인 설치가 부담스러우신 분​주방 인테리어를 화사하게 유지하고 싶으신 분​설거지 지옥에서 벗어나고 싶으신 분들께 추천합니다!

To start with the conclusion, I am so satisfied that I wonder why I didn't buy it sooner! 1. Design and Space Utilization (White is the way to go!) As expected from Bespoke, the design is incredibly clean and pretty. It doesn't detract from the kitchen interior; instead, it brightens up the space. I was worried that the 6-place setting might be too big, but placing it on one side of the sink makes it fit perfectly, like custom-made furniture. The white color makes the kitchen look spacious and is the epitome of cleanliness. 2. Capacity and Storage (Sufficient for a family of four!) If you think of it as only suitable for a single person living alone just because it's a 6-place setting, you're mistaken. The interior space is deeper and more efficiently organized than expected. If you arrange rice bowls, soup bowls, pots, and pans in the bottom section, quite a lot fits inside. The top section has a separate space to spread out cutlery and cooking utensils, ensuring they don't get tangled and are cleaned thoroughly. It fits all the dishes left after a family meal in one go. 3. Washing and Drying Performance. The most important factor is washing power, and it cleans much more thoroughly and leaves a squeaky clean finish than hand washing. Even greasy grilled meat dishes or pots with burnt-on sauce disappear without a trace if you put them in after just a light pre-wash. Since it uses high-temperature washing, it feels like it is sterilizing, so I feel much more at ease regarding hygiene. If you leave the door open after it is finished, it dries completely and is spotless. 4. Satisfaction with Rocket Installation Service. I ordered via Coupang Rocket Installation, but it was delayed by about two days, which was a bit disappointing. Overall Review and Recommendation. Since dishwashing time has decreased, I have more personal time after meals, and my quality of life as a housewife has skyrocketed. I recommend this to those who find built-in installation burdensome, those who want to keep their kitchen interior bright and cheerful, and those who want to escape the hell of dishwashing!
Comments (Original): 이사하면서 주방 가전 중 가장 고민했던 게 식기세척기였어요. 빌트인은 싱크대 하부장을 짜야 해서 번거롭고 공간도 애매했는데, 싱크대 위에 올려두고 쓰는 카운터탑 모델이 있다고 해서 폭풍 검색 끝에 비스포크로 결정했습니다. 결론부터 말씀드리면 '왜 이제 샀나' 싶을 정도로 대만족입니다!​1. 디자인 및 공간 활용 (화이트는 진리!)​역시 비스포크답게 디자인이 정말 깔끔하고 예쁩니다. 주방 인테리어를 해치지 않고 오히려 화사해진 느낌이에요. 6인용이라 너무 크지 않을까 걱정했는데, 싱크대 한쪽에 올리니 맞춤 가구처럼 딱 들어맞네요. 화이트 컬러라 주방이 넓어 보이고 깔끔함 그 자체입니다.​2. 용량 및 수납력 (4인 가족도 충분!)​6인용이라고 해서 자취생용 정도로 생각하시면 오산이에요. 생각보다 내부 공간이 깊고 알차게 구성되어 있습니다.​아래쪽엔 밥공기, 국그릇, 냄비나 프라이팬까지 요리조리 배치하면 꽤 많이 들어가요.​상단에는 수저나 조리도구를 펼쳐놓을 수 있는 공간이 따로 있어서 엉키지 않고 깨끗하게 세척됩니다.가족들이 한 끼 먹고 난 후의 설거지거리는 한 번에 다 들어가는 수준이에요.​3. 세척력 및 건조 성능​제일 중요한 건 세척력인데, 손설거지보다 훨씬 깨끗하고 뽀득뽀득하게 닦입니다. 기름기 많은 고기 구워 먹은 접시나 양념이 눌어붙은 냄비도 애벌설거지 살짝만 해서 넣으면 흔적도 없이 번쩍번쩍해져요. 고온 세척이라 살균되는 기분이라 위생적으로도 훨씬 안심이 됩니다. 완료된 후에 문을 열어두면 물기 없이 뽀송하게 말라 있어요.​4. 로켓설치 서비스 만족도​쿠팡 로켓설치로 주문했지만 이틀정도 지연되어 조금 아쉬웠어요.​ 총평 및 추천설거지 시간이 줄어드니까 식사 후에 개인 시간도 늘어나고 주부 삶의 질이 수직 상승했습니다.​빌트인 설치가 부담스러우신 분​주방 인테리어를 화사하게 유지하고 싶으신 분​설거지 지옥에서 벗어나고 싶으신 분들께 추천합니다!

However, I heard there were countertop models that sit right on the counter, so after a frantic search, I decided on the Bespoke. To start with the conclusion, I am so satisfied that I wonder why I didn't buy it sooner! 1. Design and Space Utilization (White is the way to go!) As expected from Bespoke, the design is incredibly clean and pretty. It doesn't detract from the kitchen interior; instead, it brightens up the space. I was worried that the 6-place setting might be too big, but placing it on one side of the sink makes it fit perfectly, like custom-made furniture. The white color makes the kitchen look spacious and is the epitome of cleanliness. 2. Capacity and Storage (Sufficient for a family of four!) If you think of it as only suitable for a single person living alone just because it's a 6-place setting, you're mistaken. The interior space is deeper and more efficiently organized than expected. If you arrange rice bowls, soup bowls, pots, and pans in the bottom section, quite a lot fits inside. The top section has a separate space to spread out cutlery and cooking utensils, ensuring they don't get tangled and are cleaned thoroughly. It fits all the dishes left after a family meal in one go. 3. Washing and Drying Performance. The most important factor is washing power, and it cleans much more thoroughly and leaves a squeaky clean finish than hand washing. Even greasy grilled meat dishes or pots with burnt-on sauce disappear without a trace if you put them in after just a light pre-wash. Since it uses high-temperature washing, it feels like it is sterilizing, so I feel much more at ease regarding hygiene. If you leave the door open after it is finished, it dries completely and is spotless. 4. Satisfaction with Rocket Installation Service. I ordered via Coupang Rocket Installation, but it was delayed by about two days, which was a bit disappointing. Overall Review and Recommendation. Since dishwashing time has decreased, I have more personal time after meals, and my quality of life as a housewife has skyrocketed. I recommend this to those who find built-in installation burdensome, those who want to keep their kitchen interior bright and cheerful, and those who want to escape the hell of dishwashing!
Comments (Original): 이사하면서 주방 가전 중 가장 고민했던 게 식기세척기였어요. 빌트인은 싱크대 하부장을 짜야 해서 번거롭고 공간도 애매했는데, 싱크대 위에 올려두고 쓰는 카운터탑 모델이 있다고 해서 폭풍 검색 끝에 비스포크로 결정했습니다. 결론부터 말씀드리면 '왜 이제 샀나' 싶을 정도로 대만족입니다!​1. 디자인 및 공간 활용 (화이트는 진리!)​역시 비스포크답게 디자인이 정말 깔끔하고 예쁩니다. 주방 인테리어를 해치지 않고 오히려 화사해진 느낌이에요. 6인용이라 너무 크지 않을까 걱정했는데, 싱크대 한쪽에 올리니 맞춤 가구처럼 딱 들어맞네요. 화이트 컬러라 주방이 넓어 보이고 깔끔함 그 자체입니다.​2. 용량 및 수납력 (4인 가족도 충분!)​6인용이라고 해서 자취생용 정도로 생각하시면 오산이에요. 생각보다 내부 공간이 깊고 알차게 구성되어 있습니다.​아래쪽엔 밥공기, 국그릇, 냄비나 프라이팬까지 요리조리 배치하면 꽤 많이 들어가요.​상단에는 수저나 조리도구를 펼쳐놓을 수 있는 공간이 따로 있어서 엉키지 않고 깨끗하게 세척됩니다.가족들이 한 끼 먹고 난 후의 설거지거리는 한 번에 다 들어가는 수준이에요.​3. 세척력 및 건조 성능​제일 중요한 건 세척력인데, 손설거지보다 훨씬 깨끗하고 뽀득뽀득하게 닦입니다. 기름기 많은 고기 구워 먹은 접시나 양념이 눌어붙은 냄비도 애벌설거지 살짝만 해서 넣으면 흔적도 없이 번쩍번쩍해져요. 고온 세척이라 살균되는 기분이라 위생적으로도 훨씬 안심이 됩니다. 완료된 후에 문을 열어두면 물기 없이 뽀송하게 말라 있어요.​4. 로켓설치 서비스 만족도​쿠팡 로켓설치로 주문했지만 이틀정도 지연되어 조금 아쉬웠어요.​ 총평 및 추천설거지 시간이 줄어드니까 식사 후에 개인 시간도 늘어나고 주부 삶의 질이 수직 상승했습니다.​빌트인 설치가 부담스러우신 분​주방 인테리어를 화사하게 유지하고 싶으신 분​설거지 지옥에서 벗어나고 싶으신 분들께 추천합니다!

Comments (English): [ The functionality is very poor. ] || ---------------- || Dishwashers are supposed to clean by washing with detergent and rinsing. After using it, I found that detergent residue remains on the surface of the dishes after running the standard cycle. Even after completely hand-washing the dishes and running the machine without detergent, residue remains. Detergent residue from the previous cycle stays at the back. The service representative claimed that using liquid detergent would prevent residue from remaining. I filmed 150 videos and sent them to the representative. They sent the videos to the headquarters in China to verify the operation method, came to inspect the machine, and left after stating there were no issues with its operation. Despite two service visits, there has been absolutely no improvement. When I stated that I wanted a performance inspection and a full recall of this product from the Consumer Protection Agency, Coupang contacted me the very next day offering a refund. I declined the refund to preserve evidence, but the government agency stated they are processing the matter, and I have received no further news. Problems: 1. Rinsing does not occur at all after washing. 2. Detergent residue appears even during subsequent washes. 3. Since there is no water jet spraying from above, and cleaning is performed by water sprayed from below hitting the ceiling and dripping, it does not clean effectively. 4. Due to the direction of the water stream, grease is not washed away well even when the appropriate amount of detergent is applied. Please remember that if you use this without thinking due to issues with its function and structure, you may end up ingesting a large amount of detergent powder. While using liquid detergent makes detergent stains less visible, it would be a big mistake to assume that there are no detergent residues.

Sentence (English): I purchased the beige color to match the kitchen's atmosphere, and I am truly satisfied with the design.
Comments (English): I purchased the beige color to match the kitchen's atmosphere, and I am truly satisfied with the design. As it is part of the Objet Collection, it blends naturally into the kitchen, and installing it as a built-in unit makes it look much cleaner. Since it is a 14-place setting model, the interior is more spacious than I expected, and being able to fit pots and pans has significantly reduced dishwashing time. I am particularly satisfied with how well it cleans greasy dishes and rice bowls, and I liked that the steam function allows for hygienic use. At first, I wondered if a dishwasher would really be convenient, but after using it, I understand why it is necessary. Since I can just put the dishes in and run it right after a meal, the kitchen always stays tidy. The operating noise is not as loud as I expected, and I am also satisfied that not much water remains after drying. It doesn't take up much space in a 26-pyeong kitchen, and since it is installed as a built-in unit, it maximizes space utilization.

Sentence (English): The dishwasher itself is OK, except for a couple of annoyances.
Comments (English): [ Dishwasher good, but installer was not ] || ---------------- || The dishwasher itself is OK, except for a couple of annoyances. As others mentioned, the bottom rack can slide off easily. But this seems to be a common "feature" these days as companies decide a sturdy rail would be too "unsightly". This is what comes of arrogantly ignorant MBAs running companies and favoring form over function. The other annoying thing is that it turns off automatically when you open it at the end of a cycle. I like to leave it on as an indication that the dishwasher is now clean. But otherwise it seems to do a good job.But my main gripe is about the installer. First of all, I never received a call or text with my delivery window. On the morning of the delivery I called and was informed that my window was 1 - 4 pm. However the installers showed up at noon when I was not at home.They told my daughter that the water supply valve under the sink was still running even when closed and so they could not install the dishwasher unless it was replaced. When I got home I found that there was just a small trickle coming from the valve when closed. I then shut off the main valve for the house (stopping the flow completely) and proceeded to install the dishwasher myself.I find it surprising that the installers could not have done the same thing. Instead they expected me to call a plumber and fix something that was not a problem unless the valve was closed with no supply line connected -- a problem which arises only when installing a dishwasher, and one which could be easily worked around by shutting off the main water valve.I think Costco needs to stop working with these installers before they tarnish Costco's reputation. I am already having second thoughts about buying more appliances from Costco, wondering if I will get the same clueless installers again for something I cannot handle myself.

Sentence (English): After my trusted Bosch dishwasher gave out after 22 years, I decided to replace it with a brand new LG 24-Inch Smart FlushFit™.
Comments (English): [ Dead in two weeks and nonexistent customer care ] || ---------------- || After my trusted Bosch dishwasher gave out after 22 years, I decided to replace it with a brand new LG 24-Inch Smart FlushFit™. That was a massive mistake. Delivered at the end of April, the dishwasher died after just two weeks. When the first LG technician arrived, he spent less than three minutes in my house before lazily blaming a "voltage issue" and telling me to call an electrician. I did, which cost me out-of-pocket, and my electrician confirmed the wiring and voltage were absolutely perfect. After complaining about being misdiagnosed, LG assigned me a representative named John from their "Presidential Liaison" team. Rather than getting executive treatment, the service plummeted. John routinely ignores follow-ups and takes days to respond. Since then, a second technician came out and found a broken control board. It took five business days for the part to arrive and be replaced. The moment it was fixed and turned on? A brand new error code appeared: the heat sensor was also broken. We then had to wait another full week for the new sensor to arrive. A technician finally installed it, and while the machine is technically working now, this relentless cycle of repairs left us without a dishwasher for two solid months.I understand that technology can occasionally fail out of the box. What I cannot accept is a company refusing to replace a clearly faulty, brand-new appliance, forcing the customer to endure endless repairs, and assigning a "liaison" who does absolutely nothing to manage the situation. I recently bought an LG washer and dryer as well, but this experience has completely ruined the brand for me. You learn the true quality of a company when things go wrong, and LG has failed miserably. Avoid their appliances; the customer care is nonexistent.

Comments (English): [ It's Just Right ] || ---------------- || My dishwasher died, so after doing a bit of research, we drove to Lowe's and were assited by Cheyanne who was knowledgable about the pros and cons of the various brands and models. We settled on the KitchenAid as it appeared to be "just right" on desired featuers, and those we didn't need. My husband installed it and the only downside was the instructions were a little sparse for drain and electrical hookups. So far I am totally in love with this dishwasher. We needed it to heat water plus have a good heated drying cycle, plus we have an open kitchen so low noise while washing was paramount. It washes the dishes really well and is so quiet we have to check to ensure it's running. The only downisde is it takes 4 hours to run a cyle with a normal wash with drying and sanitizing, It also has the features of delaying the wash and popping open when it's finished. One issue to watch for is although the instructions advise cleaning the filtire every 4-5 weeks but my advice would be to do it every 4-5 days to avoid build-up.

Sentence (English): After using the LG dishwasher knife and scissors holder, I found it to be more useful in the kitchen than I expected.
Comments (English): After using the LG dishwasher knife and scissors holder, I found it to be more useful in the kitchen than I expected. However, it is advisable to check the size, as very large or thick knives may be difficult to hold. Overall, I consider it an accessory that enhances both safety and convenience. It is a product I would recommend to anyone who frequently washes knives and scissors in their dishwasher.

Comments (English): [ You May End Up Washing Your Dishes by Hand ] || ---------------- || ⚠️ You May End Up Washing Your Dishes by Hand.I have owned this dishwasher for more than 1.5 years. The chemical odor has been present since the very first day, and despite promising to help, LG never provided a solution.In May, I described this issue in a review. LG responded, provided contact information, and gave me hope that the problem would finally be resolved.I contacted them and spent a considerable amount of time answering questions and providing additional information.Then. nothing.More than a month has passed. No one has called, no one has followed up, and no solution has been offered.I specifically chose a dishwasher with a stainless steel interior because I wanted as little plastic inside the appliance as possible. After extensive testing, I found that the strongest chemical odor appears to come from the black rubber door gasket. Every time the dishwasher runs, it produces a smell resembling heated rubber, vinyl, petroleum products, or synthetic plastic.The odor fills the entire first floor of our home and sometimes even reaches the second floor. About three months ago, I stopped using the dishwasher completely, even though it is still relatively new.I cannot identify exactly which compounds are responsible for this odor. However, it is clearly a strong chemical smell—not something that should normally be present in a home. We all know that heating plastics and synthetic materials can release potentially harmful fumes. That raises an obvious question: has anyone evaluated what may be released from this rubber gasket during normal dishwasher operation, and whether breathing these emissions every day for months or years is safe? If this same rubber gasket or similar material is used in other LG dishwasher models, I sincerely hope the company investigates this issue carefully. Based on my experience, I encourage future buyers to pay close attention to any chemical odor during the first few uses and not assume it will simply disappear over time.Today I still have a relatively new dishwasher that I no longer use because I am deeply concerned about my family—especially my child—breathing this chemical odor every day.As a paying customer, I fulfilled my part by purchasing a brand-new appliance. Instead, my family spent more than a year and a half living with this persistent chemical odor. Now I am faced with the choice of either washing dishes by hand or spending even more money to replace a dishwasher that is still practically new. That is incredibly disappointing.

Sentence (English): Review of a product I bought with my own money.
Comments (English): Review of a product I bought with my own money. 1. There is no "Quick" cycle available. I consider this a major drawback. To compensate, there is a "Sterilization Dry" cycle that includes a high-temperature rinse (75°C) and a 50-minute drying-only cycle. 2. The hot air drying cycle can be disabled. I ran the sterilization drying cycle, went out, and when I returned, the automatic door had opened and the dishes were dry. 3. The energy efficiency rating is Grade 4. It is not great. Perhaps it is because the hot air drying includes a high-temperature rinse. I chose this model because having fluffy, dry dishes is so important to me that I used a separate hot air dryer before this dishwasher. 4. The top rack can be removed to accommodate bulky items. 5. Although there is an "Add Rinse" button, the "Powerful" cycle consists of one wash followed by four rinses; it cleans well. 6. The drain strainer is stainless steel and easy to attach and detach. However, after using it for a few months, I want to return it and buy a different product. The plate rack is spaced too closely together, so the thick plates I have at home do not fit. Consequently, only a few dishes can fit in the rack. It stacks the bowls one on top of the other like Tetris, and it doesn't come out neat.

Sentence (English): I finally decided to bite the bullet and buy this dishwasher thanks to a promotion.
Comments (English): I finally decided to bite the bullet and buy this dishwasher thanks to a promotion. It is last year's model, but I chose it for its functionality and great value for money. Thanks to my son's love for me and his financial support, I was able to escape the kitchen. The technician came and worked for two hours in over 30-degree weather, and he installed it beautifully, neatly, and precisely in the exact location I wanted. It looked so hot that I tried to turn on a fan for him, but he said it was fine because dust would fly around while he was cutting the wooden boards; however, watching him made us feel a bit uncomfortable. There are three types of shelves, so the space is spacious enough that even if a family of three piles up dishes all day, it doesn't get full. The water pressure is strong, and it features hot air drying and automatic door opening. I think I need to study the functions a bit more. It is great that I can download settings to configure the functions I want and prefer. There were several types of dedicated detergents, but I ordered the solid type because it seemed more convenient. With a reasonable price and friendly service, my satisfaction is top-notch.
Comments (Original): 식기세척기행사로 큰 맘먹고 구매했네요.모델은 작년거지만 기능적인면과 가격가성비로 아들의 엄마 사랑에 머니 지원으로 주방탈출을 하게되었어요.기사님 오셔서 30도 넘는 날씨에  2시간의 공사에 예쁘고 제가 원하던  위치에 깔끔하고 정확히 설치해주셨어요.너무 더워보여서 선풍기 틀어드리려니 나무판 자르는데 먼지 날리다면서 괜찮다는데 보고있는 저희는 맘이 쫌 불편했네요.선반이 3종류라서 세식구 하루 종일 설거지 모아도 다 차지않을만큼 공간이 넓더라구요.물쌀도 쎄고, 열풍건조에 자동문열림등기능은 공부를 좀 해야할것같네요.다운로드 받아서 원하는 기능과 선호기능을 셋팅할수 있어서 좋아요.전용세제도 종류가 여러이던데,고체형이 좀더 편해보여서  주문했어요.착한가격에 친절한 서비스로 만족도 최곱니다.

Sentence (English): I'd don't know what the deal is with the other reviews on Costco's website: this dishwasher is great.
Comments (English): I'd don't know what the deal is with the other reviews on Costco's website: this dishwasher is great. Look up on YouTube or Reddit for reviews for dishwashers and Bosch comes out solidly on top and this is one of the best. I also saw some data from Consumer Reports and literally the top 20 dishwashers they recommended were all Bosch, so that's why I bought this one, despite weirdly negative reviews from Costco customers. Anyways, I've been really happy with it. I'm in AZ with well water and it cleans well even with the super hard water. The third rack for silverware is awesome and let's me load more than my previous dishwasher. It also looks great and is quiet. If you live in a dry climate like AZ, the auto air feature is a game changer for dry dishes cause it leverages your already dry climate to dry them more without costing any energy. I've also been really happy with the app. It was easy to set up, provides helpful maintenance and cleaning reminders, and provides a bunch of advanced options unavailable through the panel. We did have an issue that when Costco installed it, the technician discovered some part of the door was scraping and grinding. But the technician discovered it after he installed it, had us use that unit for a week, and scheduled it to be replaced with a new one the next week, so Costco's commitment to quality really showed up. No complaints at all. I will agree with some of the harsher reviews that the tines are kind of close together on the bottom rack, but I've found that if you load it the way Bosch recommends, you can load the dishes super dense (i.e. like 6 bowls only about an inch apart) and they still somehow all get clean. The adjustable middle rack is also way more useful than I expected to accommodate taller objects.

Sentence (English): #SamsungElectronicsEventParticipation.
Comments (English): #SamsungElectronicsEventParticipation. I had been using a competitor's 2-tier, 6-place setting dishwasher for 5 years without any issues, but after experiencing water leakage for about a year, I switched to this Samsung dishwasher. There were also many discontinued 6-place setting models, so the selection was limited. Perhaps because it is a single-tier model, it seems to hold a larger amount of laundry. I have been using it for over a month, and the basic wash cycle takes about 1 hour and 30 minutes. That feels too long (companies took about 1 hour). So, I found that the "Powerful" cycle takes about 1 hour! I am using that setting. Also, competitor models had a standard hot air function, but Samsung separates this feature by model, so I chose a model that includes a hot air drying function! Hmm. I am currently using it with the hot air set to low. There is definitely a difference in the size of water droplets depending on whether the hot air is used or not (I think it is better to use it). Another thing that surprised me is that the door doesn't open after the wash cycle is finished; instead, it opens automatically about 20 minutes beforehand and the sound of the hot air drying starts playing. I'd say this was the most unique aspect. Competitor models used to finish everything internally before the door would snap open at the very end. I can't help but compare them. My previous dishwasher had water leaking into the panel, so I'm worried that this Samsung dishwasher might have the same issue. I hope it stays sturdy and lasts for over 7 years! (I accidentally broke a part while applying too much force to run it on the first day, and I'm not sure who I should call.)

Sentence (English): Real review.
Comments (English): [ I could manage without it, but it would be incredibly difficult to lose it after having it. ] || ---------------- || Real review. Used for 3-4 days. Cleaning power: 5 out of 5. I tried to run various tests, but I haven't yet tried things like burnt marks on frying pans or completely dried-out rice grains stuck on. I've only used the 1-hour cycle, but dishes that were generally used and roughly rinsed with water were 100% perfectly clean. I used only one mini tablet of Frosh Green Lemon detergent. I put in about 5 rice bowls, 4 soup bowls, 1 frying pan, 5 cutlery sets, 1 medium-sized pot, 2 side dish containers, 2 slightly larger side dish bowls, and 6 cups. They all came out perfectly clean with just one mini tablet on the 1-hour cycle. Downside: It feels like a waste of detergent for running small loads. It cleans well regardless of how greasy the dishes are. By nature, I usually pre-wash dishes with water before placing them in the sink, but this time I rinsed them even more roughly with water just to remove any color from seasonings before putting them in. I just throw in greasy items as long as the color isn't visible. Even so, it cleans incredibly well—though I assume it depends on the detergent. Based on using Frosh detergent, when the door opens after a 1-hour cycle, there is almost no water left except for the grooved areas facing upwards. If I run it before bed, everything is dry by morning. Even if I take them out immediately after the 1-hour cycle, there is hardly any water. Dishes without grooves or cutlery are dry enough to be put away right away. I searched extensively on YouTube and in reviews to find answers to questions about cleaning power, and regarding comments about rice grains remaining, I think they fall into one of three categories: 1. Cases where completely dry rice grains are stuck, or eating habits where a lot of rice is left in the bowl without pre-washing. 2. Using a mild detergent. 3. Cases where dishes are piled high after eating 2 or 3 meals a day, preventing the water from properly reaching the rice grains. The washing process is quite quiet; while you can hear the sound of water splashing against the walls when rinsing or when the water jets powerfully spray, it isn't loud. It seems like the more dishes there are, the quieter it gets. The sound of water hitting the walls is the loudest. At first, the one-hour time felt long, but if you get distracted for even a moment, it's over. There are various cycles available, but without adding any options, the one-hour cycle is set to one hour. The standard cycle is displayed as 3 hours and 40 minutes, and the intensive cycle as 2 hours and 40 minutes. If you feel uneasy about the one-hour cycle and plan to use a different one, it will take a bit longer. Even the shortest cycle downloaded via LG Sync was 1 hour and 40 minutes. The manual states that the standard cycle reduces electricity consumption by slowly heating the water or something similar, but I don't think I'll ever need to use that. The design isn't as pretty as I expected; it looks like a mini refrigerator. I've heard so much about how great dishwashers are, and while I'm confused by the various reviews and opinions, having one is definitely convenient. With a family of six, washing dishes usually takes about 20 minutes on days with little to 30-40 minutes, but it is much more convenient to just put everything in and run it for an hour. The kids use a new cup every time they drink water, so the pile of cups is insane; I used to be stressed about washing them, but that stress disappeared instantly. You don't really need anything else; it is a must-have for any household where washing dishes takes about 30 minutes. Actually, 30 minutes is the washing itself, but if you add in the time for drying and tidying up, an hour feels like nothing. With the dishwasher, I just run the 1-hour cycle and don't really care whether I clean up or not. I usually just clear away the pots and pans and use the rest of the dishes immediately for the next meal, so it doesn't take any extra time. Also, I don't see a single grain of rice in the food strainer—perhaps because the water jet blows away soaked rice or rice from dishes I just ate from, turning it into powder and disappearing.

Sentence (English): I've only used the 1-hour cycle, but dishes that were generally used and roughly rinsed with water were 100% perfectly clean.
Comments (English): [ I could manage without it, but it would be incredibly difficult to lose it after having it. ] || ---------------- || Real review. Used for 3-4 days. Cleaning power: 5 out of 5. I tried to run various tests, but I haven't yet tried things like burnt marks on frying pans or completely dried-out rice grains stuck on. I've only used the 1-hour cycle, but dishes that were generally used and roughly rinsed with water were 100% perfectly clean. I used only one mini tablet of Frosh Green Lemon detergent. I put in about 5 rice bowls, 4 soup bowls, 1 frying pan, 5 cutlery sets, 1 medium-sized pot, 2 side dish containers, 2 slightly larger side dish bowls, and 6 cups. They all came out perfectly clean with just one mini tablet on the 1-hour cycle. Downside: It feels like a waste of detergent for running small loads. It cleans well regardless of how greasy the dishes are. By nature, I usually pre-wash dishes with water before placing them in the sink, but this time I rinsed them even more roughly with water just to remove any color from seasonings before putting them in. I just throw in greasy items as long as the color isn't visible. Even so, it cleans incredibly well—though I assume it depends on the detergent. Based on using Frosh detergent, when the door opens after a 1-hour cycle, there is almost no water left except for the grooved areas facing upwards. If I run it before bed, everything is dry by morning. Even if I take them out immediately after the 1-hour cycle, there is hardly any water. Dishes without grooves or cutlery are dry enough to be put away right away. I searched extensively on YouTube and in reviews to find answers to questions about cleaning power, and regarding comments about rice grains remaining, I think they fall into one of three categories: 1. Cases where completely dry rice grains are stuck, or eating habits where a lot of rice is left in the bowl without pre-washing. 2. Using a mild detergent. 3. Cases where dishes are piled high after eating 2 or 3 meals a day, preventing the water from properly reaching the rice grains. The washing process is quite quiet; while you can hear the sound of water splashing against the walls when rinsing or when the water jets powerfully spray, it isn't loud. It seems like the more dishes there are, the quieter it gets. The sound of water hitting the walls is the loudest. At first, the one-hour time felt long, but if you get distracted for even a moment, it's over. There are various cycles available, but without adding any options, the one-hour cycle is set to one hour. The standard cycle is displayed as 3 hours and 40 minutes, and the intensive cycle as 2 hours and 40 minutes. If you feel uneasy about the one-hour cycle and plan to use a different one, it will take a bit longer. Even the shortest cycle downloaded via LG Sync was 1 hour and 40 minutes. The manual states that the standard cycle reduces electricity consumption by slowly heating the water or something similar, but I don't think I'll ever need to use that. The design isn't as pretty as I expected; it looks like a mini refrigerator. I've heard so much about how great dishwashers are, and while I'm confused by the various reviews and opinions, having one is definitely convenient. With a family of six, washing dishes usually takes about 20 minutes on days with little to 30-40 minutes, but it is much more convenient to just put everything in and run it for an hour. The kids use a new cup every time they drink water, so the pile of cups is insane; I used to be stressed about washing them, but that stress disappeared instantly. You don't really need anything else; it is a must-have for any household where washing dishes takes about 30 minutes. Actually, 30 minutes is the washing itself, but if you add in the time for drying and tidying up, an hour feels like nothing. With the dishwasher, I just run the 1-hour cycle and don't really care whether I clean up or not. I usually just clear away the pots and pans and use the rest of the dishes immediately for the next meal, so it doesn't take any extra time. Also, I don't see a single grain of rice in the food strainer—perhaps because the water jet blows away soaked rice or rice from dishes I just ate from, turning it into powder and disappearing.

I put in about 5 rice bowls, 4 soup bowls, 1 frying pan, 5 cutlery sets, 1 medium-sized pot, 2 side dish containers, 2 slightly larger side dish bowls, and 6 cups. Based on using Frosh detergent, when the door opens after a 1-hour cycle, there is almost no water left except for the grooved areas facing upwards. If I run it before bed, everything is dry by morning. Even if I take them out immediately after the 1-hour cycle, there is hardly any water. Dishes without grooves or cutlery are dry enough to be put away right away. I searched extensively on YouTube and in reviews to find answers to questions about cleaning power, and regarding comments about rice grains remaining, I think they fall into one of three categories: 1. Cases where completely dry rice grains are stuck, or eating habits where a lot of rice is left in the bowl without pre-washing. 2. Using a mild detergent. 3. Cases where dishes are piled high after eating 2 or 3 meals a day, preventing the water from properly reaching the rice grains. The washing process is quite quiet; while you can hear the sound of water splashing against the walls when rinsing or when the water jets powerfully spray, it isn't loud. It seems like the more dishes there are, the quieter it gets. The sound of water hitting the walls is the loudest. At first, the one-hour time felt long, but if you get distracted for even a moment, it's over. There are various cycles available, but without adding any options, the one-hour cycle is set to one hour. The standard cycle is displayed as 3 hours and 40 minutes, and the intensive cycle as 2 hours and 40 minutes. If you feel uneasy about the one-hour cycle and plan to use a different one, it will take a bit longer. Even the shortest cycle downloaded via LG Sync was 1 hour and 40 minutes. The design isn't as pretty as I expected; it looks like a mini refrigerator. I've heard so much about how great dishwashers are, and while I'm confused by the various reviews and opinions, having one is definitely convenient. You don't really need anything else; it is a must-have for any household where washing dishes takes about 30 minutes. Actually, 30 minutes is the washing itself, but if you add in the time for drying and tidying up, an hour feels like nothing. I put in about 5 rice bowls, 4 soup bowls, 1 frying pan, 5 cutlery sets, 1 medium-sized pot, 2 side dish containers, 2 slightly larger side dish bowls, and 6 cups. Based on using Frosh detergent, when the door opens after a 1-hour cycle, there is almost no water left except for the grooved areas facing upwards. If I run it before bed, everything is dry by morning. Even if I take them out immediately after the 1-hour cycle, there is hardly any water. Dishes without grooves or cutlery are dry enough to be put away right away. I searched extensively on YouTube and in reviews to find answers to questions about cleaning power, and regarding comments about rice grains remaining, I think they fall into one of three categories: 1. Cases where completely dry rice grains are stuck, or eating habits where a lot of rice is left in the bowl without pre-washing. 2. Using a mild detergent. 3. Cases where dishes are piled high after eating 2 or 3 meals a day, preventing the water from properly reaching the rice grains. The washing process is quite quiet; while you can hear the sound of water splashing against the walls when rinsing or when the water jets powerfully spray, it isn't loud. It seems like the more dishes there are, the quieter it gets. The sound of water hitting the walls is the loudest. At first, the one-hour time felt long, but if you get distracted for even a moment, it's over. There are various cycles available, but without adding any options, the one-hour cycle is set to one hour. The standard cycle is displayed as 3 hours and 40 minutes, and the intensive cycle as 2 hours and 40 minutes. If you feel uneasy about the one-hour cycle and plan to use a different one, it will take a bit longer. Even the shortest cycle downloaded via LG Sync was 1 hour and 40 minutes. The manual states that the standard cycle reduces electricity consumption by slowly heating the water or something similar, but I don't think I'll ever need to use that. The design isn't as pretty as I expected; it looks like a mini refrigerator. I've heard so much about how great dishwashers are, and while I'm confused by the various reviews and opinions, having one is definitely convenient. With a family of six, washing dishes usually takes about 20 minutes on days with little to 30-40 minutes, but it is much more convenient to just put everything in and run it for an hour. You don't really need anything else; it is a must-have for any household where washing dishes takes about 30 minutes. Actually, 30 minutes is the washing itself, but if you add in the time for drying and tidying up, an hour feels like nothing. I usually just clear away the pots and pans and use the rest of the dishes immediately for the next meal, so it doesn't take any extra time. I tried to run various tests, but I haven't yet tried things like burnt marks on frying pans or completely dried-out rice grains stuck on. I've only used the 1-hour cycle, but dishes that were generally used and roughly rinsed with water were 100% perfectly clean. I used only one mini tablet of Frosh Green Lemon detergent. I put in about 5 rice bowls, 4 soup bowls, 1 frying pan, 5 cutlery sets, 1 medium-sized pot, 2 side dish containers, 2 slightly larger side dish bowls, and 6 cups. They all came out perfectly clean with just one mini tablet on the 1-hour cycle. Downside: It feels like a waste of detergent for running small loads. It cleans well regardless of how greasy the dishes are. By nature, I usually pre-wash dishes with water before placing them in the sink, but this time I rinsed them even more roughly with water just to remove any color from seasonings before putting them in. Based on using Frosh detergent, when the door opens after a 1-hour cycle, there is almost no water left except for the grooved areas facing upwards. If I run it before bed, everything is dry by morning. Even if I take them out immediately after the 1-hour cycle, there is hardly any water. Dishes without grooves or cutlery are dry enough to be put away right away. I searched extensively on YouTube and in reviews to find answers to questions about cleaning power, and regarding comments about rice grains remaining, I think they fall into one of three categories: 1. Cases where completely dry rice grains are stuck, or eating habits where a lot of rice is left in the bowl without pre-washing. 2. Using a mild detergent. 3. Cases where dishes are piled high after eating 2 or 3 meals a day, preventing the water from properly reaching the rice grains. The washing process is quite quiet; while you can hear the sound of water splashing against the walls when rinsing or when the water jets powerfully spray, it isn't loud. It seems like the more dishes there are, the quieter it gets. The sound of water hitting the walls is the loudest. At first, the one-hour time felt long, but if you get distracted for even a moment, it's over. There are various cycles available, but without adding any options, the one-hour cycle is set to one hour. The standard cycle is displayed as 3 hours and 40 minutes, and the intensive cycle as 2 hours and 40 minutes. If you feel uneasy about the one-hour cycle and plan to use a different one, it will take a bit longer. Even the shortest cycle downloaded via LG Sync was 1 hour and 40 minutes. The manual states that the standard cycle reduces electricity consumption by slowly heating the water or something similar, but I don't think I'll ever need to use that. The design isn't as pretty as I expected; it looks like a mini refrigerator. I've heard so much about how great dishwashers are, and while I'm confused by the various reviews and opinions, having one is definitely convenient. With a family of six, washing dishes usually takes about 20 minutes on days with little to 30-40 minutes, but it is much more convenient to just put everything in and run it for an hour. The kids use a new cup every time they drink water, so the pile of cups is insane; I used to be stressed about washing them, but that stress disappeared instantly. You don't really need anything else; it is a must-have for any household where washing dishes takes about 30 minutes. Actually, 30 minutes is the washing itself, but if you add in the time for drying and tidying up, an hour feels like nothing. With the dishwasher, I just run the 1-hour cycle and don't really care whether I clean up or not. I usually just clear away the pots and pans and use the rest of the dishes immediately for the next meal, so it doesn't take any extra time. Also, I don't see a single grain of rice in the food strainer—perhaps because the water jet blows away soaked rice or rice from dishes I just ate from, turning it into powder and disappearing.

Comments (English): [ I could manage without it, but it would be incredibly difficult to lose it after having it. ] || ---------------- || Real review. Used for 3-4 days. Cleaning power: 5 out of 5. I tried to run various tests, but I haven't yet tried things like burnt marks on frying pans or completely dried-out rice grains stuck on. I've only used the 1-hour cycle, but dishes that were generally used and roughly rinsed with water were 100% perfectly clean. I used only one mini tablet of Frosh Green Lemon detergent. I put in about 5 rice bowls, 4 soup bowls, 1 frying pan, 5 cutlery sets, 1 medium-sized pot, 2 side dish containers, 2 slightly larger side dish bowls, and 6 cups. They all came out perfectly clean with just one mini tablet on the 1-hour cycle. Downside: It feels like a waste of detergent for running small loads. It cleans well regardless of how greasy the dishes are. By nature, I usually pre-wash dishes with water before placing them in the sink, but this time I rinsed them even more roughly with water just to remove any color from seasonings before putting them in. I just throw in greasy items as long as the color isn't visible. Even so, it cleans incredibly well—though I assume it depends on the detergent. Based on using Frosh detergent, when the door opens after a 1-hour cycle, there is almost no water left except for the grooved areas facing upwards. If I run it before bed, everything is dry by morning. Even if I take them out immediately after the 1-hour cycle, there is hardly any water. Dishes without grooves or cutlery are dry enough to be put away right away. I searched extensively on YouTube and in reviews to find answers to questions about cleaning power, and regarding comments about rice grains remaining, I think they fall into one of three categories: 1. Cases where completely dry rice grains are stuck, or eating habits where a lot of rice is left in the bowl without pre-washing. 2. Using a mild detergent. 3. Cases where dishes are piled high after eating 2 or 3 meals a day, preventing the water from properly reaching the rice grains. The washing process is quite quiet; while you can hear the sound of water splashing against the walls when rinsing or when the water jets powerfully spray, it isn't loud. It seems like the more dishes there are, the quieter it gets. The sound of water hitting the walls is the loudest. At first, the one-hour time felt long, but if you get distracted for even a moment, it's over. There are various cycles available, but without adding any options, the one-hour cycle is set to one hour. The standard cycle is displayed as 3 hours and 40 minutes, and the intensive cycle as 2 hours and 40 minutes. If you feel uneasy about the one-hour cycle and plan to use a different one, it will take a bit longer. Even the shortest cycle downloaded via LG Sync was 1 hour and 40 minutes. The manual states that the standard cycle reduces electricity consumption by slowly heating the water or something similar, but I don't think I'll ever need to use that. The design isn't as pretty as I expected; it looks like a mini refrigerator. I've heard so much about how great dishwashers are, and while I'm confused by the various reviews and opinions, having one is definitely convenient. With a family of six, washing dishes usually takes about 20 minutes on days with little to 30-40 minutes, but it is much more convenient to just put everything in and run it for an hour. The kids use a new cup every time they drink water, so the pile of cups is insane; I used to be stressed about washing them, but that stress disappeared instantly. You don't really need anything else; it is a must-have for any household where washing dishes takes about 30 minutes. Actually, 30 minutes is the washing itself, but if you add in the time for drying and tidying up, an hour feels like nothing. With the dishwasher, I just run the 1-hour cycle and don't really care whether I clean up or not. I usually just clear away the pots and pans and use the rest of the dishes immediately for the next meal, so it doesn't take any extra time. Also, I don't see a single grain of rice in the food strainer—perhaps because the water jet blows away soaked rice or rice from dishes I just ate from, turning it into powder and disappearing.

Comments (English): [ I could manage without it, but it would be incredibly difficult to lose it after having it. ] || ---------------- || Real review. Used for 3-4 days. Cleaning power: 5 out of 5. I searched extensively on YouTube and in reviews to find answers to questions about cleaning power, and regarding comments about rice grains remaining, I think they fall into one of three categories: 1. Cases where dishes are piled high after eating 2 or 3 meals a day, preventing the water from properly reaching the rice grains. Dishes without grooves or cutlery are dry enough to be put away right away. I searched extensively on YouTube and in reviews to find answers to questions about cleaning power, and regarding comments about rice grains remaining, I think they fall into one of three categories: 1. Cases where completely dry rice grains are stuck, or eating habits where a lot of rice is left in the bowl without pre-washing. 2. Using a mild detergent. 3. Cases where dishes are piled high after eating 2 or 3 meals a day, preventing the water from properly reaching the rice grains. The washing process is quite quiet; while you can hear the sound of water splashing against the walls when rinsing or when the water jets powerfully spray, it isn't loud. At first, the one-hour time felt long, but if you get distracted for even a moment, it's over. Dishes without grooves or cutlery are dry enough to be put away right away. I searched extensively on YouTube and in reviews to find answers to questions about cleaning power, and regarding comments about rice grains remaining, I think they fall into one of three categories: 1. Cases where completely dry rice grains are stuck, or eating habits where a lot of rice is left in the bowl without pre-washing. 2. Using a mild detergent. 3. Cases where dishes are piled high after eating 2 or 3 meals a day, preventing the water from properly reaching the rice grains. The washing process is quite quiet; while you can hear the sound of water splashing against the walls when rinsing or when the water jets powerfully spray, it isn't loud. It seems like the more dishes there are, the quieter it gets. The sound of water hitting the walls is the loudest. At first, the one-hour time felt long, but if you get distracted for even a moment, it's over. You don't really need anything else; it is a must-have for any household where washing dishes takes about 30 minutes. Actually, 30 minutes is the washing itself, but if you add in the time for drying and tidying up, an hour feels like nothing. Comments (English): [ I could manage without it, but it would be incredibly difficult to lose it after having it. ] || ---------------- || Real review. Used for 3-4 days. Cleaning power: 5 out of 5. I tried to run various tests, but I haven't yet tried things like burnt marks on frying pans or completely dried-out rice grains stuck on. I've only used the 1-hour cycle, but dishes that were generally used and roughly rinsed with water were 100% perfectly clean. I used only one mini tablet of Frosh Green Lemon detergent. I put in about 5 rice bowls, 4 soup bowls, 1 frying pan, 5 cutlery sets, 1 medium-sized pot, 2 side dish containers, 2 slightly larger side dish bowls, and 6 cups. It cleans well regardless of how greasy the dishes are. Based on using Frosh detergent, when the door opens after a 1-hour cycle, there is almost no water left except for the grooved areas facing upwards. If I run it before bed, everything is dry by morning. Even if I take them out immediately after the 1-hour cycle, there is hardly any water. Dishes without grooves or cutlery are dry enough to be put away right away. I searched extensively on YouTube and in reviews to find answers to questions about cleaning power, and regarding comments about rice grains remaining, I think they fall into one of three categories: 1. Cases where completely dry rice grains are stuck, or eating habits where a lot of rice is left in the bowl without pre-washing. 2. Using a mild detergent. 3. Cases where dishes are piled high after eating 2 or 3 meals a day, preventing the water from properly reaching the rice grains. The washing process is quite quiet; while you can hear the sound of water splashing against the walls when rinsing or when the water jets powerfully spray, it isn't loud. It seems like the more dishes there are, the quieter it gets. The sound of water hitting the walls is the loudest. At first, the one-hour time felt long, but if you get distracted for even a moment, it's over. There are various cycles available, but without adding any options, the one-hour cycle is set to one hour. The standard cycle is displayed as 3 hours and 40 minutes, and the intensive cycle as 2 hours and 40 minutes. If you feel uneasy about the one-hour cycle and plan to use a different one, it will take a bit longer. Even the shortest cycle downloaded via LG Sync was 1 hour and 40 minutes. The manual states that the standard cycle reduces electricity consumption by slowly heating the water or something similar, but I don't think I'll ever need to use that. The design isn't as pretty as I expected; it looks like a mini refrigerator. I've heard so much about how great dishwashers are, and while I'm confused by the various reviews and opinions, having one is definitely convenient. With a family of six, washing dishes usually takes about 20 minutes on days with little to 30-40 minutes, but it is much more convenient to just put everything in and run it for an hour. The kids use a new cup every time they drink water, so the pile of cups is insane; I used to be stressed about washing them, but that stress disappeared instantly. You don't really need anything else; it is a must-have for any household where washing dishes takes about 30 minutes. Actually, 30 minutes is the washing itself, but if you add in the time for drying and tidying up, an hour feels like nothing. With the dishwasher, I just run the 1-hour cycle and don't really care whether I clean up or not. I usually just clear away the pots and pans and use the rest of the dishes immediately for the next meal, so it doesn't take any extra time. Also, I don't see a single grain of rice in the food strainer—perhaps because the water jet blows away soaked rice or rice from dishes I just ate from, turning it into powder and disappearing.

Comments (English): [ I could manage without it, but it would be incredibly difficult to lose it after having it. ] || ---------------- || Real review. Used for 3-4 days. Cleaning power: 5 out of 5. I tried to run various tests, but I haven't yet tried things like burnt marks on frying pans or completely dried-out rice grains stuck on. I've only used the 1-hour cycle, but dishes that were generally used and roughly rinsed with water were 100% perfectly clean. I used only one mini tablet of Frosh Green Lemon detergent. I put in about 5 rice bowls, 4 soup bowls, 1 frying pan, 5 cutlery sets, 1 medium-sized pot, 2 side dish containers, 2 slightly larger side dish bowls, and 6 cups. It cleans well regardless of how greasy the dishes are. Based on using Frosh detergent, when the door opens after a 1-hour cycle, there is almost no water left except for the grooved areas facing upwards. If I run it before bed, everything is dry by morning. Even if I take them out immediately after the 1-hour cycle, there is hardly any water. Dishes without grooves or cutlery are dry enough to be put away right away. I searched extensively on YouTube and in reviews to find answers to questions about cleaning power, and regarding comments about rice grains remaining, I think they fall into one of three categories: 1. Cases where completely dry rice grains are stuck, or eating habits where a lot of rice is left in the bowl without pre-washing. 2. Using a mild detergent. 3. Cases where dishes are piled high after eating 2 or 3 meals a day, preventing the water from properly reaching the rice grains. The washing process is quite quiet; while you can hear the sound of water splashing against the walls when rinsing or when the water jets powerfully spray, it isn't loud. It seems like the more dishes there are, the quieter it gets. The sound of water hitting the walls is the loudest. At first, the one-hour time felt long, but if you get distracted for even a moment, it's over. There are various cycles available, but without adding any options, the one-hour cycle is set to one hour. The standard cycle is displayed as 3 hours and 40 minutes, and the intensive cycle as 2 hours and 40 minutes. If you feel uneasy about the one-hour cycle and plan to use a different one, it will take a bit longer. Even the shortest cycle downloaded via LG Sync was 1 hour and 40 minutes. The design isn't as pretty as I expected; it looks like a mini refrigerator. I've heard so much about how great dishwashers are, and while I'm confused by the various reviews and opinions, having one is definitely convenient. With a family of six, washing dishes usually takes about 20 minutes on days with little to 30-40 minutes, but it is much more convenient to just put everything in and run it for an hour. The kids use a new cup every time they drink water, so the pile of cups is insane; I used to be stressed about washing them, but that stress disappeared instantly. You don't really need anything else; it is a must-have for any household where washing dishes takes about 30 minutes. Actually, 30 minutes is the washing itself, but if you add in the time for drying and tidying up, an hour feels like nothing. With the dishwasher, I just run the 1-hour cycle and don't really care whether I clean up or not. I usually just clear away the pots and pans and use the rest of the dishes immediately for the next meal, so it doesn't take any extra time. Also, I don't see a single grain of rice in the food strainer—perhaps because the water jet blows away soaked rice or rice from dishes I just ate from, turning it into powder and disappearing.
